5241)    Excess Current Phase R of Rotor

5242)    Excess Current Phase S of Rotor
Description: This alarm is triggered if the control system detects an overcurrent in one of the
inverter phases lasting longer than 1ms.

Digital variable EIntRotR or EIntRotS change to one, depending on which phase the error
occurred.

Possible causes:

  CCU
  Inverter driver
  Inverter IGBTs
  Inverter current sensors (CTs)
  Interface board (U3) or its cables
  Passive or Smart crowbar
  Generator

Troubleshooting steps:

It is advised to use OCS configurator to record and view the actual value and set points for the
Rectifier and Inverter currents, DC Bus voltage, and stator currents to see what is happening at
the time of the fault. The recording trigger should be set to EIntRotR =1 or EIntRotS =1
depending on what phase the fault is occurring. The pre-trigger should be set to 90%. In
addition to the recommended analog variables, the default 32 digital variables should also be
recorded.

The inverter drivers, IGBTs and current sensors should all be inspected. These may be
interchanged between phases if needed to see if the fault moves.

The wiring interface board should also be inspected, along with the wiring and connections of
the current sensors to the interface board.

If this alarm occurs very frequently or during the Pole Angle Test, you can try disconnecting the
Smart and/or Passive crowbars to check if either one is causing the fault. It is recommended to
disconnect the smart crowbar first in order to rule it out. This is because it is not possible to
disconnect the passive crowbar without also disconnecting the smart crowbar, so it would not
be possible to determine which is at fault. To disconnect the smart crowbar, you need to
disconnect the two yellow cables connected to the passive crowbar rectifier bridge buss bars.

INGETEAM CONVERTER V3.3 (GAMESA) TROUBLESHOOTING MANUAL Page 49 of 70

The wind turbine should then be started (or the Pole Angle Test run, if the alarm occurs during
the test) and if the fault does not re-occur then the problem lies in the smart crowbar. If this is
the case, you should inspect and test the components of the smart crowbar for damage.

If the smart crowbar is causing the fault and cannot be replaced or repaired immediately, then
it can be disabled to allow the turbine to run. Keep in mind that if there is a grid voltage dip the
turbine will go into emergency. To disable the smart crowbar, leave the two yellow cables
disconnected from the passive crowbar and use OCS or TFL to change the parameter Crow_En
to zero.

If the fault persists, the next step is to disconnect the passive crowbar to check if the diodes or
thyristor are shorting out. This can be done by disconnecting the passive crowbar supply cables
from the rotor inductor L3. In the picture below, these are the three green cables coming from
above along the right side of the inductor:





    INGETEAM CONVERTER V3.3 (GAMESA) TROUBLESHOOTING MANUAL    Page 50 of 70

The Pole Angle Test can be run, and if the fault does not re-occur then the problem lies in the
passive crowbar. If this is the case, inspect and test the passive crowbar components for
damage. Note: the turbine should NOT be started with the passive crowbar disconnected, as
the converter would not have any protection from grid voltage failure.

If the fault still persists, then the rotor of the generator should be checked. The rotor insulation
should be tested (megger test) and phase-to-phase resistance tested to check for leakages that
could cause the overcurrent. To do this, disconnect the rotor cables from the rotor inductor L3
and test with a Megohmeter set to 1KV range. Insulation test results (phase to ground) should
be higher than 200 mega ohms. Resistance should be checked with a normal multi-meter, the
readings between each of the three phases should be similar. If any of the readings are out of
range, the generator should be checked (including the slip ring and brushes).

IMPORTANT: The Passive crowbar can only be disconnected for testing. If the problem is found
to be in one of the components of the passive crowbar then it should be repaired before
restarting the turbine. The turbine should never be operated without the passive crowbar
protection.









    INGETEAM CONVERTER V3.3 (GAMESA) TROUBLESHOOTING MANUAL    Page 51 of 70

5243)        Excess Current Phase R of Stator
5244)        Excess Current Phase S of Stator
Description: This alarm is triggered if the control system detects an overcurrent in the stator
phase R or S lasting 1ms.

Digital variable EInStaR or EInStaS change to one, depending on which phase the overcurrent
was detected.

Possible causes:

     Inverter drivers
     Inverter or Stator current sensors
     Inverter IGBTs
     CCU

Troubleshooting steps:

The first step for troubleshooting this alarm, before replacing any components, should be to
use the OCS configurator to record the rotor and stator currents and generator speed in order
to see their values at the time of the fault. The recording trigger should be set to EInStaR = 1 or
EInStaS = 1, depending on which phase the fault occurred. The pre-trigger should be set to
90%. Once a recording has been saved, it should be analyzed to help determine the cause of the
fault:

If there are no readings on one of the Stator current sensors and an overcurrent in the other
phases, then you need to check that sensor and its connection to the CCU. It is also possible
that the CCU is not measuring correctly. To check this, swap current sensors between phases.

If the Inverter or rotor currents appear abnormal right before the stator overcurrent, then you
should focus on resolving this fault be following the steps listed for the alarm "Overcurrent in a
rotor phase".

When the Passive Crowbar is triggered and closes, it will often cause an overcurrent in the
stator. In this case, the alarm "5213- Crowbar overvoltage" will appear along with "stator
overcurrent" and you should focus on resolving the DC bus overvoltage.









INGETEAM CONVERTER V3.3 (GAMESA) TROUBLESHOOTING MANUAL    Page 52 of 70
